neighbours.label: The frequency adverb 'often' (including 'more often than not' and pre-nominal 'often overlooked'); weaker on synonyms, quiet on other frequency words such as rarely, sometimes, seldom, never.
fire: My grandmother told us that story often, usually on rainy evenings.
Small businesses, more often than not, fail within their first five years.
The charity supports refugees and other often forgotten communities.
In winter the roads are often closed because of heavy snow.
Students who sleep well often perform better on exams.
The painter often worked through the night in his small studio.
These symptoms are often mistaken for a common cold.
Travellers often complain about the long queues at the border.
quiet: My grandmother told us that story once, on a rainy evening.
Small businesses, in a few cases, fail within their first five years.
The charity supports refugees and other recently arrived communities.
In winter the roads are sometimes closed because of heavy snow.
Students who sleep well rarely perform worse on exams.
The painter never worked through the night in his small studio.
These symptoms are seldom mistaken for a common cold.
Travellers occasionally complain about the long queues at the border.

predictions: median fire ~0.85 (probes: 0.98, 0.92, 0.78); near misses < 0.25 (sometimes 0.17, rarely 0.15, 'in most cases' 0.03). 'frequently' 0.46 and 'common' 0.34 were left out of the near misses.
notes: Card: ' often' x21, ' Common' x4, Japanese 'よく', Russian 'чаще'. Distinction is high frequency vs other frequencies.
